alternatives.argument: Count all vertex slots to get 4V=2I+E. Build a spanning tree from a first vertex by adding an edge to one new vertex at a time; it has V−1 edges. Each remaining internal edge adds one cycle, including a self-loop or a parallel edge, so L=I−V+1. Substitute I=(4V−E)/2 and L=I−V+1 into the defined degree DL−2I to obtain D+(D−4)V−(D−2)E/2; setting D=4 gives 4−E. This is only the declared superficial power count.

The local definition explicitly fixes a finite connected multigraph with V≥1 four-slot vertices, counts self-loops twice, defines external half-edges, states L=I−V+1, assigns +D per loop measure and −2 per scalar propagator, and records the formal-only limitation. It needs no outside proof supplier.

For two quartic vertices joined by two internal edges with two external half-edges at each vertex, V=2, I=2, E=4, and L=1. The quartic-degree proposition gives ω4=4L−2I=0. Separately and conditionally, assume AC and instantiate the actual QFT-IR04 anomaly statement with u(x)=1/(16π^4|x|^4), its smooth compact cutoff χ=1 near zero, and positive μ,ν; the exact scale-change formula and no-homogeneous-extension conclusion follow as that premise. The two calculations are not identified with an integrated graph amplitude and assert no convergence or divergence.

alternatives.argument: Count all vertex slots to get 4V=2I+E. Build a spanning tree from a first vertex by adding an edge to one new vertex at a time; it has V−1 edges. Each remaining internal edge adds one cycle, including a self-loop or a parallel edge, so L=I−V+1. Substitute I=(4V−E)/2 and L=I−V+1 into the defined degree DL−2I to obtain D+(D−4)V−(D−2)E/2; setting D=4 gives 4−E. This is only the declared superficial power count.

Assign degree −1 to coordinates, +1 to derivatives, −D to the measure, and zero to the action. The kinetic monomial forces 2+2[φ]=D, hence [φ]=(D−2)/2; degree zero of g_r φ^r d^Dx forces [g_r]=D−r(D−2)/2. Under φ_b(x)=b^{−(D−2)/2}φ(x/b), chain rule and x=by give invariant kinetic term and monomial exponent D−r(D−2)/2. No quantum correction or fixed point is inferred.
